prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on your trip. Choose an Airbnb (cabin, lakefront cottage, condo) if you want privacy, space, a kitchen and a local feel; choose a hotel if you want convenience, predictable service, on‑site amenities (pool, spa, front desk, packages) and easier last‑minute booking. Below is a quick guide plus specific, well‑reviewed options for common needs.

Which to pick — pros & cons
- Airbnb (cabin/condo/house)
  - Pros: more space, kitchen, better for groups/families, lakefront or secluded Ozark cabins, often better value per person.
  - Cons: variable quality, extra cleaning/service fees, parking or HOA rules, check‑in can be self‑check-in, less predictable service.
- Hotel / resort
  - Pros: consistent service, on‑site restaurants/spa/pools, concierge can book shows/tours, loyalty/points, often easier if you want packages or short stays.
  - Cons: less space, can be pricier per person, fewer “local home” vibes.

Where to stay by priority
- Branson Strip / Hwy 76 (best for shows, restaurants, family attractions): stay in a hotel or condo within walking distance of theaters and attractions.
- Branson Landing / Downtown (best for shopping, lakefront dining, easy walking): hotels and condos on the Landing are convenient.
- Silver Dollar City / West Branson (best for theme‑park days): look for cabins or condos within 10–15 minutes of Silver Dollar City.
- Table Rock Lake / Indian Point / Kimberling City / Hollister (best for boating, fishing, lake views): lakefront cabins, private homes or resort condos.
- Ozark cabins / Big Cedar area (best for nature, hiking, luxury lodge experience): cabins and resorts close to outdoor activities.

Specific places (good starting recommendations)
Hotels & resorts
- Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — upscale, lakefront, full spa and pools; great for couples and anyone wanting a resort feel.
- Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — excellent location on Branson Landing (walk to shops, dining, fountains), lake views and convenient downtown access.
- The Keeter Center at College of the Ozarks — unique, high‑quality lodging and farm‑to‑table dining; quieter and well maintained.
- Big Cedar Lodge (near Branson, in Ridgedale) — top pick if you want luxury lodge amenities and outdoor activities; a short drive from Branson.
- Welk Resort Branson — condo style rooms, good for families and longer stays; often includes pools and on‑site entertainment.
- Grand Country Inn & Waterpark — family‑oriented, affordable, attached to family attractions and shows.

Airbnb types & areas to search
- Table Rock Lake cabin / lakefront cottage — look in Indian Point, Kimberling City, Hollister for docks, boat access, firepit, and big decks.
- Ozark log cabin with hot tub — for couples or small groups wanting seclusion and views.
- Branson Landing condo or Loft — if you want walkability to restaurants and evening entertainment.
- Large family homes close to Hwy 76 / the Strip — convenient for shows and attractions.

Practical tips when choosing
- Ask: how many people, dates, budget, priorities (lake vs shows vs quiet)? I can tailor picks if you tell me those.
- If booking Airbnb: filter for Entire place, Superhost, free cancellation if possible, instant book if you prefer, read recent reviews (last 90 days), check parking and HOA/rental rules, confirm docking/boat rules if lakefront.
- If booking a hotel: check if they include parking, breakfast, pool access (seasonal), and if they have show/package deals or shuttle service.
- Consider drive time: Branson’s attractions are spread out — Silver Dollar City is west, Branson Landing downtown, Table Rock Lake south/west. A car is helpful unless you stay right on the Landing.
- Seasonal: summer and fall (leaf season) are busiest—book early. Winter can be quieter and cheaper, but some condos/pools may be closed.

Price ranges (approximate)
- Budget hotel / motel: $70–120/night (off‑season cheaper)
- Midrange hotel / condo: $120–250/night
- Upscale resort / lakefront cabin: $200–500+/night (Big Cedar & Chateau higher end)
- Airbnbs: studios/1BR $80–150; cabins/2–4BR $120–400+ depending on lakefront and season.

If you tell me: dates, party size, and whether you prefer lake access, being in walking distance to shows, or a secluded cabin, I’ll give 3–5 specific current options (one hotel, one resort, and a couple of Airbnb/cabin suggestions) and point to good neighborhoods to target.
